items.title: Security
items.text:
• /mcp does not use the browser login or CSRF token. It needs Authorization: Bearer <token>; a missing or wrong token gets 401.
  • While the switch is off, /mcp answers 404.
  • A request carrying another site's Origin header is refused with 403, which blocks DNS-rebinding attacks from a browser.
  • Behind a reverse proxy, pass the Host header through (see self-hosting.md) so the Origin check compares against the public name.
  • Pick the smallest profile that does the job. Full lets an agent delete papers and projects permanently.
  • In multi-user mode only admins can change the MCP settings or create the token, and /mcp always works on the owner's library. The shared and per-account libraries are out of its reach. See Server Admin.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Probe the endpoint by hand. Streamable HTTP needs the Mcp-Session-Id returned by initialize on every later request:

URL=http://127.0.0.1:8086/mcp
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN"
ACCEPT="Accept: application/json, text/event-stream"
CT="Content-Type: application/json"

SID=$(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "$URL" -H "$AUTH" -H "$ACCEPT" -H "$CT" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"0"}}}' \
  | tr -d '\r' | awk -F': ' 'tolower($1)=="mcp-session-id"{print $2}')

curl -s -X POST "$URL" -H "$AUTH" -H "$ACCEPT" -H "$CT" -H "Mcp-Session-Id: $SID" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}'

curl -s -X POST "$URL" -H "$AUTH" -H "$ACCEPT" -H "$CT" -H "Mcp-Session-Id: $SID" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  | jq -r '.result.tools[] | "\(.name)\t\(.annotations.readOnlyHint)\t\(.annotations.destructiveHint)"'
Reply Cause 404 on every request MCP switched off in Settings, or wrong path 401 Missing, wrong, replaced or revoked token 403 Request carries a different site's Origin 400 Missing Mcp-Session-Id Request after initialize without the session header 404 with a session id Session closed (idle, replaced token, restart); initialize again Tool not available on this server Tool is outside the chosen profile or always blocked

The current session count shows on the Settings card.

items.title: Cleaning up PDF file names before an import
items.text:
PDF collections often have file names with spaces, accents, Greek letters, curly quotes or dashes copied from a title. Some disks, shells and sync tools handle those badly. scripts/sanitize-pdf-names.py renames every PDF under a folder to a plain ASCII name, so the files are easy to handle before you import them with bulk import or upload them.

Run it before the import, on a folder linXiv does not know yet. linXiv stores the path of each PDF it links. A file renamed after it was imported loses its link: the paper shows no PDF, and Server Admin → Check PDF files lists it as missing. This matters most for --place in-situ imports, which link your own files where they are.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.8 or newer on the machine that holds the folder. It uses the standard library only, so nothing needs installing. Debian, Ubuntu and macOS ship a suitable python3.
  • Write access to the folder.

The script never talks to the linXiv-web server, so the container can be running or stopped.

items.title: Getting the script onto the server
items.text:
scp scripts/sanitize-pdf-names.py server:linxiv-web/
ssh server 'chmod +x linxiv-web/sanitize-pdf-names.py'

Then, on the server:

cd linxiv-web
./sanitize-pdf-names.py --help

items.title: Dry run
items.text:
By default the script only lists what it would do:

./sanitize-pdf-names.py /mnt/usb/Papers

sanitize-pdf-names dry run: /mnt/usb/Papers
RENAME 2019/β-cell αβ – “study”.pdf -> 2019/beta-cell_alphabeta-study.pdf
RENAME 2021/Résumé & notes.PDF -> 2021/Resume_and_notes.pdf
RENAME misc/same name.pdf -> misc/same_name_2.pdf
DELETE .DS_Store
SKIP   readme.txt (not a PDF)
3 rename(s), 1 macOS junk file(s) to delete, 1 non-PDF skipped
dry run: nothing changed. Re-run with --apply.

Every run also writes its output to ./sanitize-pdf-names-<date>-<time>.log, or to the file given with --log FILE.

items.title: Renaming
items.text:
./sanitize-pdf-names.py --apply /mnt/usb/Papers

Each rename is logged as OK or FAIL. The script also writes rename-manifest-<date>-<time>.tsv in the folder, one old<TAB>new line per rename (paths relative to the folder). Keep it until you are sure about the result.

The exit code is 0 when every rename worked, 1 when one or more failed, and 2 for a bad argument or a refused folder.

items.title: Undoing a run
items.text:
./sanitize-pdf-names.py --undo rename-manifest-20261101-120000.tsv /mnt/usb/Papers

The script reads the manifest backwards and gives each file its old name back. A file that is missing, or whose old name is taken again, is reported as SKIP and left alone. Deleted macOS junk files are not restored.

items.title: Rename rules
items.text:
• Names keep A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - only. Spaces and any other character become _, and repeated _ collapse into one.
  • Greek letters are spelled out (β to beta, Ω to Omega, the micro sign µ to mu).
  • Unicode dashes become -. Quotes, ™ ® © and invisible characters are dropped. ß æ ø ł þ & and similar become ss ae o l th and. Other accented letters lose their accent (é to e); letters with no ASCII form are dropped.
  • .PDF becomes .pdf. A file with no extension that starts with %PDF- gets .pdf. Other files are reported as SKIP and keep their names.
  • When two files in one folder clean to the same name, the later ones get _2, _3 and so on. Case is ignored for this, because exFAT and macOS disks treat A.pdf and a.pdf as the same file. Nothing is ever overwritten.
  • Names are cut at 200 characters before .pdf. A name with nothing left becomes unnamed.pdf.
  • Folder names are never changed. Hidden files (names starting with .) are left alone, except .DS_Store and ._* AppleDouble files, which --apply deletes.

linXiv-web reads a title from the file name when a PDF carries none: it splits the name on _, and drops a trailing _2 style suffix. The rules above keep names in that shape.

items.title: Inside a linXiv library
items.text:
The script refuses a folder that holds a papers.db, or sits anywhere under a folder that does, such as the PDF folder inside the linXiv data directory:

sanitize-pdf-names: /srv/linxiv/data/pdfs is inside the linXiv library at /srv/linxiv/data. Renaming its files would unlink their papers' PDFs. Run it on a folder before importing it, or add --force.

--force runs it anyway and logs a WARN line. Only use it when you know none of the files are linked yet. A PDF folder kept on another disk (LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST) has no papers.db next to it, so the script can't tell it is a library: check the path yourself.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Message Meaning a folder is required Give the folder as the last argument. not a directory: … The path does not exist or is a file. … is inside the linXiv library at … See Inside a linXiv library. FAIL … appeared meanwhile Another program created a file with the new name during the run. Run the script again. FAIL …: [Errno 13] Permission denied The folder is not writable for your user. SKIP … (target exists) during --undo The old name is taken by another file. Rename that file, then run the undo again; finished lines are skipped as missing.

items.title: Server scripts
items.text:
Command-line helpers for jobs that are too big for the web UI. Copy one to the machine that hosts the linXiv-web container (or holds your PDFs), make it executable, and start with --help. The shell scripts need sh, curl and jq; the Python one needs python3.

Script What it does Page scripts/sanitize-pdf-names.py Renames the PDFs under a folder to plain ASCII file names, with a dry run first and an undo manifest. Run it before importing the folder. Sanitize PDF file names scripts/bulk-import.sh Imports a folder of PDFs that is already on the server: through the running server, or offline with the container stopped, copying, moving or linking the files where they are. Bulk PDF import scripts/bulk-ai-tags.sh Asks the AI set up in Settings → AI for tags for every paper that has none (or every paper with --all) and adds them. Bulk AI tags scripts/export-tags.sh Writes every paper's tags to a CSV, one row per paper per tag, that can be used to put the tags back. Export tags

For a large collection, the usual order is:

  1. sanitize-pdf-names.py on the folder (dry run, then --apply).
  2. bulk-import.sh on the same folder.
  3. bulk-ai-tags.sh for the papers that came in without tags.
  4. export-tags.sh to keep a copy of the tags.

Every script has a dry run or changes nothing until told to, and each writes a log next to where it runs.

items.title: Self-hosting linXiv-web with Docker
items.text:
This guide runs linXiv-web on your own machine or home server from the prebuilt container image. For development and building from source, see Development.

The current release is the release branch, published as the image tag used below. main may contain changes that are not released yet.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Docker with Docker Compose v2 (docker compose), on Linux, macOS or Windows.
  • An amd64 or arm64 machine. The image is published for both.
  • Two directories on the host: one for the library database, one for PDFs.

The image bundles the linxiv CLI and linxiv-mcp, built from linXiv v0.7.1. Do not point linXiv-web at a data directory that the linXiv desktop app or linxiv-headless also uses: linXiv expects one process per library.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
mkdir -p linxiv-web/data linxiv-web/pdfs
cd linxiv-web

On Linux, the container runs as uid 1000 and must be able to write both directories:

sudo chown 1000:1000 data pdfs

Create docker-compose.yml:

services:
  linxiv-web:
    image: ghcr.io/toledoem/linxiv-web:0.1.4
    container_name: linxiv-web
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    ports:
      # 127.0.0.1 = this machine only. Use 0.0.0.0 to reach it from the LAN.
      - "${LINXIV_WEB_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT:-8086}:8000"
    volumes:
      # Long syntax: a missing host directory is an error, not a silently created empty one.
      - type: bind
        source: ${LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST:-./data}
        target: /data
        bind:
          create_host_path: false
      - type: bind
        source: ${LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST:-./pdfs}
        target: /pdfs
        bind:
          create_host_path: false
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health')"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

Start it:

docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f linxiv-web

Open http://127.0.0.1:8086.

The image is tagged with the linXiv-web version (0.1.4) and latest; pin the version to choose when you update. The image is public: no docker login needed.

items.title: First-run setup
items.text:
With no password configured, the server starts in setup mode and logs:

linxiv-web: no password set; first-run setup is open on 0.0.0.0:8000. The first visitor creates the admin password.

The first person to open the web UI creates the admin password (at least 8 characters) and is logged in. Until then every API call is refused. Do the setup before you publish the port to a network you don't trust.

After the password, the wizard offers optional steps, each with Skip:

  1. Contact emails for arXiv, Crossref and OpenAlex, and an NCBI (PubMed) API key.
  2. Theme and light/dark mode (stored in the browser).
  3. AI provider, model and key (off by default).
  4. Home feed URL and PDF folder layout.

Everything in the wizard can be changed later in Settings.

The password hash is stored in data/linxiv-web-auth.json (mode 0600). linXiv-web never stores the password itself.

items.title: Setting the password in .env instead
items.text:
A password from the environment always wins over the stored one, and setup never opens. Generate an argon2 hash:

docker run --rm -e PASSWORD='your-password' --entrypoint python \
  ghcr.io/toledoem/linxiv-web:0.1.4 -m app hash-password

Put it in .env next to docker-compose.yml, in single quotes (the hash contains $):

LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH='$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$...'

items.title: Changing or resetting the password
items.text:
Logged in: Settings → Server & data → Login changes the password and logs out every other browser. "Log out other sessions" there ends all sessions except yours.

Forgotten password: set a new one from the server, no restart needed (every browser is logged out):

docker compose exec linxiv-web python -m app reset-password

Or remove the stored password so the next visitor runs first-run setup again (the library is untouched):

docker compose down
rm data/linxiv-web-auth.json
docker compose up -d

A password set with LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH / LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD always wins; change it in .env instead.

In multi-user mode, reset-password --user <name> resets one account's password and logs only that account out; without --user it resets the owner's server password. See Server Admin.

items.title: Logging in
items.text:
Tick Remember me on this browser to stay logged in for 90 days (LINXIV_WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS changes this). Without it, the login ends when the browser closes, and after 14 days at most.

Sessions are kept in data/linxiv-web-state.db, so restarting or updating the container keeps you logged in.

items.title: More than one person
items.text: By default linXiv-web has one password and one library. To give other people their own logins and libraries, plus a shared library that only admins change, turn on multi-user mode in Settings → Server Admin. The login page then asks for a username as well. Server Admin explains accounts, roles and the shared library.

items.title: Where your data lives
items.text:
Host directory Container Contents data/ (LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST) /data papers.db (library), user_settings.json (linXiv settings, including API keys entered in Settings), linxiv-web-auth.json (admin password hash), linxiv-web-state.db (sessions, login throttle, multi-user accounts), libraries/ (shared and per-account libraries in multi-user mode) pdfs/ (LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST) /pdfs PDFs, flat or in year/journal subfolders (Settings → Library → PDF folders)

Keep data/ on a local disk: SQLite over network shares or exFAT is unreliable. pdfs/ may live on a NAS or external drive.

To use other locations, set them in .env (both directories must exist):

LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST=/srv/linxiv/data
LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST=/mnt/nas/papers

items.title: Reaching it from other machines
items.text:
Set in .env:

LINXIV_WEB_BIND=0.0.0.0
LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT=8086

then docker compose up -d, and open http://<server-ip>:8086. This is plain HTTP: use it on a trusted LAN, or put HTTPS in front.

items.title: HTTPS with a reverse proxy
items.text:
Keep LINXIV_WEB_BIND=127.0.0.1 and let the proxy on the same host forward to it. Set in .env:

LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE=true
LINXIV_WEB_HSTS=true   # optional: browsers stop using plain HTTP for this host

The proxy must pass the original Host header: linXiv-web rejects writes whose Origin doesn't match the host it sees.

linXiv-web serves only loopback, private LAN and link-local addresses unless LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true. Behind a proxy it sees the proxy's address, so everyone passes as the proxy. To see real client addresses, list the proxy in LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES (from inside the container it usually shows up as the Docker gateway, e.g. 172.17.0.1, or the whole 172.16.0.0/12) and make it send X-Forwarded-For; then internet clients need LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true.

Caddy (passes Host by default, gets certificates itself):

papers.example.org {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8086
}

nginx:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name papers.example.org;
    # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ...
    client_max_body_size 200m;   # match LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8086;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_read_timeout 480s;  # long searches, imports, AI calls, two large add-on PDFs queued
    }
}

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Settings changed in the web UI are stored in data/. Environment variables go in .env and need docker compose up -d to apply. The most useful ones:

Variable Default Purpose LINXIV_WEB_BIND / LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT 127.0.0.1 / 8086 Where compose publishes the port LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST / LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST ./data / ./pdfs Host directories LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH none Admin password hash; skips first-run setup LINXIV_WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS 90 Login lifetime with Remember me LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE false true behind HTTPS LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL false Serve public IP addresses (else 403) LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES none Proxy IPs/CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For is believed LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB 200 Upload size cap LINXIV_WEB_LIBRARIES_PDF_DIR none Multi-user mode: PDF folder for the shared and per-account libraries (container path; mount it) CROSSREF_MAILTO, NCBI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, … none Override the values entered in Settings

The full list is in Admin Server Configuration.

items.title: Importing many PDFs
items.text: To import a folder of PDFs that is already on the server, without the web UI, use scripts/bulk-import.sh. See bulk-import.md.

items.title: Backups
items.text:
• Database only: Settings → Server & data → Backup downloads a copy of papers.db and can import or restore one. It does not include PDFs. The same card exports and imports the settings (without API keys).
  • Database copies on the server: the "Back up databases" maintenance operation keeps the newest copies of every library database inside the data directory, nightly or on demand. See Maintenance operations. Set TZ on the container so the nightly hour is your local time.
  • Everything: stop the container and copy both directories:
docker compose down
tar czf linxiv-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz data pdfs
docker compose up -d

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Change the image tag in docker-compose.yml to the new version, then:

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Reload open browser tabs with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R so they pick up the new interface.

items.title: Building the image yourself
items.text:
Instead of pulling from GHCR, compose can build from the git repository. Replace the image: line with:

    build:
      context: https://github.com/ToledoEM/linXiv-web.git#release
      args:
        LINXIV_REF: v0.7.1
    image: linxiv-web:local

and run docker compose build && docker compose up -d. The first build compiles linXiv from source and takes several minutes. To build local changes, clone the repository and use context: ./linXiv-web instead of the URL.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Fix Container exits with LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR=/pdfs is not writable (or the data dir) On Linux: sudo chown 1000:1000 data pdfs ... does not exist (mount the PDF directory) Create the host directories before starting; compose won't create them Container exits with linxiv-web-auth.json is unreadable The stored password file is damaged: delete it and run setup again invalid password after setting LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH Keep the hash in single quotes in .env; compose expands $ otherwise Writes fail with cross-origin request rejected behind a proxy The proxy must forward the original Host header 403 External requests are disabled The client has a public IP address: set LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true, or reach it over LAN/VPN Container exits with LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES: '…' is not an IP or CIDR Use addresses or CIDRs, not host names Old interface after an update Hard reload with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R Logged out after a restart LINXIV_WEB_SECRET_KEY changed, or data/linxiv-web-state.db was deleted docker compose pull says denied Log in to ghcr.io (see Quick start)

items.title: Server Admin
items.text: Out of the box linXiv-web has one password and one library. Multi-user mode adds named accounts, each with its own library, plus a shared library that everyone can read and only admins can change. It stays off until an admin turns it on, and turning it on leaves your existing library as it is.

items.title: Multi-user mode
items.text:
Open Settings → Server Admin → Multi-user mode, choose your username and click Turn on. You keep the server password (the one set in .env or during first-run setup), and your library stays your own. From then on the login page asks for a username and a password.

The account that turned the mode on is the server owner. It always stays an admin and can't be deleted.

Only the owner can turn the mode off. Everyone else is logged out at once, and afterwards only the owner can log in, with the password alone as before. Accounts, their libraries and the shared library are kept and come back when the mode is turned on again.

items.title: Accounts
items.text:
Settings → Server Admin → Users lists every account with its role, library and creation date. From there an admin can:

  • add an account with a username, a password and a role (user or admin);
  • rename an account or set a new password for it;
  • change its role;
  • delete it.

Usernames use lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 32 characters. Passwords need at least 8 characters, and no two accounts may share one, the owner's server password included.

A new password, a role change or a deletion logs that account out of every browser at once. The last admin can't be demoted or deleted, and nobody can delete their own account.

Deleting an account removes the login only. Its library stays on disk, and the panel shows the folder so you can keep, move or remove it yourself.

items.title: What admins and users can do
items.text:
User Admin Own library: add, edit, tag, projects, notes, PDFs Yes Yes Own settings: AI keys, contacts, feeds, metadata lookup Yes Yes Read the shared library and copy papers from it Yes Yes Change the shared library No Yes Change own password Yes Yes Server Admin: multi-user mode and accounts No Yes Maintenance operations and server backups No Yes Duplicates page: merge or dismiss in own library Yes Yes App logs, activity log No Yes Update check, health, disk space, diagnostics No Yes MCP server and its token No Yes Server-wide settings: log level, update check, GHCR_TOKEN, MCP No Yes

Users don't see the settings cards and groups they can't use, and the server checks the role on every request.

items.title: The shared library
items.text:
The top of the sidebar switches between My library and Shared library (M and S when the sidebar is collapsed). The choice is remembered in each browser. In the shared library a banner says which one you are looking at.

Admins fill the shared library with the usual pages: Add Paper, Search, Upload and the Home feed all work on whichever library is shown.

For users the shared library is read only. They can browse and search it, open PDFs and export BibTeX. The buttons that would change it are hidden, and the server refuses those changes.

To keep a paper, select it in the Library and click Copy to my library, or use the same button on the paper page. The paper and its PDF land in your own library, and the shared copy stays where it is. If you already have the paper, your stored metadata is kept.

items.title: How the databases relate
items.text:
Accounts and libraries live in separate files. linxiv-web-state.db holds accounts and sessions, and each account points at one library. A library is an ordinary linXiv data folder with its own papers.db, settings and PDF folder.

flowchart LR
  state[("linxiv-web-state.db<br>accounts, sessions")]
  subgraph own["Own libraries"]
    root[("data/papers.db<br>+ pdfs/<br>owner")]
    u2[("data/libraries/u2/papers.db<br>+ pdfs/<br>user u2")]
  end
  shared[("data/libraries/shared/papers.db<br>+ pdfs/")]
  state -- "owner" --> root
  state -- "account u2" --> u2
  admin([Admin]) -- "adds papers" --> shared
  shared -- "read by everyone" --> user([User])
  shared -- "Copy to my library:<br>paper + PDF" --> u2

Copy to my library goes through a project archive, the same way you would move a project by hand. The server puts the papers in a temporary project in the shared library, exports it with its PDFs, imports the archive into your library, and then deletes the temporary project on both sides. The papers themselves stay.

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant S as linXiv-web
  participant SH as Shared library
  participant MY as Your library
  B->>S: Copy to my library (paper ids)
  S->>SH: temporary project + export with PDFs
  S->>MY: import, keeping papers you already have
  S->>SH: delete temporary project
  S->>MY: delete temporary project
  S-->>B: copied, not found, PDFs skipped

items.title: Projects and reading lists
items.text: Projects and reading lists belong to one library, so accounts can't see each other's. An admin can create them in the shared library, where everyone can open them. Copying papers to your library leaves their project behind.

items.title: Passwords
items.text:
Change your own password in Settings → Server & data → Login. The owner's password is the server password: when it comes from LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH or LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD, change it in .env.

Admins set a new password for anyone in the Users panel. If nobody can log in, reset a password on the server, no restart needed:

# The owner (server password)
docker compose exec linxiv-web python -m app reset-password

# One account
docker compose exec linxiv-web python -m app reset-password --user alice

Either one logs that account out of every browser.

items.title: Where the data lives
items.text:
Path in data/ Contents papers.db, user_settings.json, pdfs/ The owner's library, as before libraries/shared/ The shared library: papers.db, user_settings.json, pdfs/ libraries/u<id>/ One account's library, same layout linxiv-web-state.db Accounts (password hashes only), sessions, the multi-user switch

Libraries are created the first time they are opened. To keep the PDFs of the shared and per-account libraries on another disk, set LINXIV_WEB_LIBRARIES_PDF_DIR; each library then links its pdfs/ to <that folder>/<library>. The folder must not be inside LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR.

Settings → Server & data → Backup backs up, imports and restores the library you are looking at. Copying the whole data/ and pdfs/ folders, as in Backups, covers every library and every account.

items.title: Maintenance operations
items.text:
Settings → Server Admin → Maintenance operations lists jobs that look after every library on the server: the owner's, the shared one and each account's. Each row has a Run button, the result of its last run, and Nightly and Monthly boxes. Operations ticked Nightly run one after another once a night at the hour picked at the top of the card. Operations ticked Monthly run at that same hour once 30 days have passed since their last run finished (a Run by hand counts); an operation that never ran goes at the next nightly hour. The hour is the server's local time; set TZ on the container (for example TZ=Europe/London) when the server should not use UTC. A running operation shows its progress in the activity tray and can be cancelled.

Operation What it does Find duplicate papers Reads every saved PDF and lists papers whose files are byte for byte the same on the Duplicates page. Only new or changed files are read again on later runs. Complete metadata of new papers For papers added since its last run that have one of the gaps ticked on its row (junk title, no authors, date, abstract, journal, DOI or BibTeX details), it looks the paper up by its own DOI or arXiv id, never by title, in the sources ticked on its row and in their order, and fills those empty fields. Stored values are kept. arXiv is asked only for arXiv papers, bioRxiv only for bioRxiv/medRxiv DOIs, Crossref and PubMed for any DOI. OpenAlex is not offered: linXiv can't look it up by an exact DOI. Refresh metadata Asks again the source each paper's metadata came from, by the paper's own id (DOI, arXiv id or OpenAlex work id), and replaces the stored title, authors, date, abstract, journal, DOI and BibTeX fields with the values it gets back. Empty values never replace stored ones, the link and tags stay, an arXiv subject code never replaces a journal, and a year-only date never replaces a full date of the same year. The source is recorded when a looked-up record is saved on the paper page or in batch edit, when a paper is added by DOI or arXiv id, and by "Complete metadata of new papers". Papers with no recorded source, or one that can't be asked again (BibTeX import, PDF file name, AI cleanup), are left alone. The option on its row picks Papers published in the last year, and preprints (arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv; the default) or Every paper with a recorded source. Check PDF files Reports papers whose PDF file is missing on disk, and PDF files in the PDF folder that no paper points at. It changes nothing. Show report lists them and breaks the folder down: files of any type, PDFs, each top-level subfolder, next to the number of papers, papers with a PDF, extra version files and PDFs of papers in the trash. Skip folders lists subfolders (for example dup, errors) that are counted but never reported as unlinked. Download full list (TSV) under each list has every missing paper or unlinked file, tab separated. Move to orphans/ checks again and moves each unlinked PDF to orphans/ under the same path; files changed in the last hour stay, and nothing is deleted. Back up databases Saves a copy of each library's database on the server and keeps the newest ones (7 unless you change it below the table). PDF files are not included. Clean authors without papers Deletes author records that no paper uses any more, for example the authors of papers deleted from the trash. linXiv refuses to delete an author still linked to a paper, so those are kept. It asks before running. Clean tags without papers Deletes tags that no paper and no project uses. Tags on papers in the trash stay, so a restored paper keeps its tags, and so do project tags such as reading-list. A tag named Untagged is always kept. It asks before running. Empty trash Deletes for good the papers that have been in the trash longer than the days typed on its row: 1 to 120, or 0 (the default) to never delete. Projects in the trash are left alone. It asks before running.

The first run of "Complete metadata of new papers" looks at papers added in the last 30 days. Papers it completes also get the record's BibTeX fields that are still empty, and its source when none is recorded. "No BibTeX details" counts a paper with no BibTeX field stored at all; such a paper is complete once the source returns any BibTeX field, and its other values are left alone.

Refresh metadata pauses one second between lookups, as the sources are shared public services; on a large library, tick it Monthly rather than Nightly. Each library's papers that were not found are listed in maintenance/metadata-refresh.json.

items.title: Duplicates
items.text: The Duplicates page (sidebar) shows the groups the last "Find duplicate papers" run found in the library you are looking at. Pick the paper to keep and click Merge into kept paper: linXiv moves the other papers' notes, highlights, projects, tags and PDFs to it, then deletes them. Not duplicates hides a group from later runs. Download list (TSV) saves every group, one row per paper, tab separated. The Library header links to the page while there are groups. In the shared library only admins can merge or dismiss.

items.title: Papers left incomplete
items.text: Papers that "Complete metadata of new papers" could not finish are listed per library. The Library header shows N to complete; the link, or Review papers left incomplete in the operation's row, selects them and opens batch edit metadata. Saving fixes a paper and drops it from the list; Skip takes it off the list too.

items.title: Database backups on the server
items.text: Below the operations, Database backups on the server lists the copies "Back up databases" made, per library, with Download and Delete. To restore one, download it, switch to that library and use Restore in Settings → Server & data → Backup. Backups and the other operation results live in maintenance/ inside each library's data folder.

items.title: Background jobs and MCP
items.text:
Background jobs run in the library they were started from, so the same job can run in two libraries at once. Users see only the jobs they started, and admins see all of them. Each library has its own full-text indexer; they take turns, so arXiv gets one request at a time.

The MCP server always works on the owner's library, and only admins can change its settings or token.

items.title: Authors
items.text:
The Authors page lists every author in the library with their ORCID and paper count. Filter by name or ORCID, hide authors with a single paper, and sort by full name or last name.

An author page shows their papers. From there you can edit the full, first and last name and the ORCID, or merge the author with a duplicate. linXiv-web suggests merge candidates, including authors with the same name.

Settings → AI → Author ORCIDs fills in missing ORCIDs from Crossref and OpenAlex, 20 authors per click.

items.title: Knowledge graph
items.text:
The graph shows papers, authors and tags as nodes. Click a node to open it, and Ctrl/Cmd+click to select papers. The side panels adjust the layout forces and filter the graph by node type (papers, authors, tags), category, PDF, date range or tag.

With thousands of papers the graph gets dense and slow. Use filters to thin it out.

Export GraphML and Export CSV download the whole graph to rebuild it in another tool. GraphML opens in Gephi, Cytoscape, yEd, igraph and NetworkX. CSV is a zip with nodes.csv (id, type, label and metadata such as DOI, tags and projects) and edges.csv (source, target, type). The side-panel filters are not applied; Hide single-paper authors is.

items.title: Tags
items.text: The Tags page lists every tag with the number of papers that carry it, plus an Untagged row. Click a tag to open the Library filtered to it.

items.title: Home feed
items.text: The home page opens with library counts (papers, PDFs, PDF coverage, categories, tags) and then the home feed.

items.title: Feeds
items.text:
The feed shows entries from up to 10 RSS or Atom feeds, for example https://rss.arxiv.org/rss/cs.LG or a bioRxiv subject feed. Add, rename, switch off or remove feeds in Settings → Library → Home feed. The cache retention setting there controls how many days of feed entries stay stored; papers you dismiss for good are always remembered.

The picker above the list shows all feeds merged, a random 10 entries, or one feed at a time. The keyword box filters the list to entries that contain every one of the comma-separated keywords.

Save and Dismiss work on arXiv entries only.

items.title: Filter rules
items.text: Filter rules hide entries before you see them. A DENY rule hides an entry when all its comma-separated keywords appear in the chosen field (title or summary). An ALLOW rule overrides a DENY match. Rules apply to every feed and live in Settings → Library → Feed filters.

items.title: Saved PDFs view
items.text: Home also has a Saved PDFs view that lists 10 to 100 saved PDFs at random, by size, or only untagged ones.

items.title: Library
items.text: The Library lists every paper, 50 per page by default, with a page-size choice at the bottom.

items.title: Searching and filtering
items.text:
The search box covers title, abstract, authors, ids, tags, notes and indexed full text. A query of 3 or more characters also searches the TeX source and PDF text that linXiv has indexed. The chips above the table filter by PDF (All, Has PDF, No PDF) and the tag menu filters by one tag or by untagged papers.

Filters, sort order and page number are kept in the address bar, so a reload or the Back button returns to the same view, and you can bookmark it.

items.title: Sorting
items.text:
Click any column header (Title, Authors, Published, Category, Tags, PDF) to sort by it, and click again to reverse. The sort menu on the right does the same for the common orders.

In Settings → Appearance → Paper tables you can hide columns, change their widths, and show the DOI under each title.

items.title: Suspect titles
items.text: Papers imported from PDFs sometimes get a junk title read from the file. linXiv-web flags those with a title? pill and shows the PDF file name under the title, so you can tell which file the row came from. Fix them with metadata lookup on the paper page or in batch edit, using "Search by PDF file name" when the file names are real titles.

items.title: Batch edit
items.text:
Tick papers and open batch edit to:

  • look up and apply metadata from Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex, PubMed or bioRxiv/medRxiv, with a field diff before anything is saved. The diff includes the BibTeX fields the source holds, marked (BibTeX). Rows whose stored value is empty come ticked; a row that would replace a stored value stays unticked until you tick it. A Crossref or OpenAlex match found by title has no BibTeX fields to show; on save linXiv-web reads them and fills the empty ones;
  • add or remove tags, or ask the AI for tags if AI features are on;
  • export the selection as a .bib file.

While a batch runs, leaving the page asks for confirmation, because leaving stops the batch.

When the maintenance operations have found something, the paper count at the top gains links: N duplicate groups opens the Duplicates page, and N to complete selects the papers whose metadata could not be completed automatically and opens batch edit metadata on them. See Maintenance operations.

items.title: Shared library
items.text: In multi-user mode the top of the sidebar switches between My library and Shared library. The shared library is read only unless you are an admin: batch edit and the project picker are hidden, and the selection bar offers Export .bib and Copy to my library, which copies the selected papers and their PDFs into your own library. See Server Admin.

items.title: Dark mode
items.text: The theme follows your system setting until you pick light or dark with the toggle at the bottom of the sidebar or in Settings → Appearance.

items.title: Paper page
items.text: Each paper has its own page with metadata, abstract, tags, projects, notes, highlights and the PDF.

items.title: Metadata
items.text:
The top block shows id, version, publication date, categories, journal and link. Edit metadata opens an editor that can look the paper up in Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex, PubMed or bioRxiv/medRxiv and show the result next to the stored values. Pick the fields to take, then save. The default lookup source and which sources are on are set in Settings → Library → Metadata lookup.

The diff also lists the BibTeX fields the source holds that linXiv has no column for, marked (BibTeX): entry type, volume, issue, pages, month, publisher, ISSN and so on. Ticked ones are saved with the record, and the BibTeX export of a Library selection writes them. BibTeX details under the abstract shows the stored ones and the Metadata source: where the record you saved last came from (Crossref, PubMed, bioRxiv, arXiv, OpenAlex, a BibTeX import, the PDF file name or AI cleanup), or "not recorded". Papers saved before this feature, or edited by hand only, show no fields and no source until a looked-up record is saved. The maintenance operation Refresh metadata asks the recorded source again.

A paper can be saved without authors; linXiv then stores the author as Unknown.

items.title: PDF reader
items.text:
View PDF opens the PDF to the right of the page. Drag the bar between the two panes to resize them; the width is remembered in your browser. Scrolling inside the PDF stays inside the PDF. On narrow screens the panes stack.

The reader has page navigation and find (Ctrl/Cmd+F or /). Select text to create a highlight. Open in new tab opens the file in the browser's own viewer. Delete PDF waits 5 seconds with an Undo button before it deletes.

items.title: Tags, projects and notes
items.text:
Add tags as a comma-separated list, or use AI Tags for suggestions when AI features are on. The Projects section adds the paper to an existing project or reading list, or creates a new one.

Notes are Markdown. Export .md saves the paper's notes for Obsidian. AI summary writes a summary from the abstract, or from the abstract plus PDF text, and saves it as a note when you ask.

items.title: Full text
items.text: For arXiv papers, Fetch TeX source downloads the LaTeX source and indexes its text for search. For other papers, Index PDF text indexes the PDF's text instead. A background worker can index all pending arXiv papers; see Settings.

items.title: Papers in the shared library
items.text: In multi-user mode, a paper opened from the shared library shows its metadata, abstract, tags and PDF, plus a Copy to my library button. Accounts that are not admins don't get the editing controls there: edit metadata, tags, projects, AI summary, PDF download or delete, full text and delete. See Server Admin.

items.title: Versions
items.text: arXiv version monitoring in Settings → Library checks saved arXiv papers for newer versions and lists each one with a link to the paper and a Dismiss button.

items.title: Projects
items.text:
The Projects page shows one card per active project, with its description and paper count. A switch shows archived projects instead, and deleted projects go to the Trash.

A project page lists its papers in the same sortable table as the Library. Add papers searches the library, and Export writes the project as:

  • .lxproj (optionally with PDFs), which another linXiv library can import;
  • BibTeX;
  • an Obsidian vault;
  • Zotero;
  • notes as a Markdown .zip.

Import... on the Projects page reads a .lxproj file. It shows a preview first and asks whether to merge with or overwrite a project of the same name.

items.title: Reading lists
items.text:
A reading list is a project tagged reading-list. Reading lists have their own page and stay off the Projects page. Open one to add papers.

Papers saved with the browser add-on land on the reading list Imported - to check (token in Settings). Check metadata on that list opens batch edit with every paper selected and Crossref as the source. Approve the changes you want, then Done takes the paper off the list; it stays in your library. Approve all skips matches found by title, because the first result may be a different paper: check those and approve them one at a time. A clip leaves a paper already in your library as it is, and adds the PDF if it has none.

linXiv keeps a per-paper reading status (unread, reading, read) only in its linxiv-headless HTTP API, not in the CLI, so linXiv-web can't show it yet. See Functions not in the CLI.

items.title: Search
items.text:
The Search page has tabs for arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref and your local library. Pick how many results you want and the sort order, then search.

Advanced opens an arXiv query builder: each clause searches all fields, title, author or abstract, and clauses combine with AND, OR or AND NOT. Results already in your library link to their paper page.

items.title: Add paper
items.text:
The Add paper page has three sections.

Add by link or identifier Paste an arXiv link or id, a DOI or doi.org link, a publisher article link (Nature, Springer, Wiley, ACS, APS, IOP, Science, PNAS and others), or a direct link to a PDF. For a PDF link the server downloads the file itself, from public hosts only and up to the upload size cap. Upload PDF files Drop PDFs or choose them. linXiv reads the metadata from each PDF and adds the paper with its PDF. Import a metadata file A BibTeX .bib file or a Zotero CSL JSON export. Only metadata is imported, no PDFs. Entries already in the library are updated, and papers in the trash are restored.

To import a whole folder of PDFs that is already on the server, use the bulk import script. To save the page or PDF open in Firefox, use the browser add-on.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Settings are split into groups listed on the left. The selected group lists its cards below it; click one to jump to it. Each card has its own Save button. You can link to a group directly, for example /settings#ai, or to a card in it, for example /settings#server/backup.

Settings marked as stored in the browser (theme, zoom, density, sidebar pages, paper table columns) apply to that browser only. Everything else is stored on the server.

items.title: Appearance
items.text: Theme, light/dark/system mode, zoom and density. Display turns TeX rendering in titles and abstracts on or off. Sidebar picks which pages appear in the sidebar; Home, Library, Projects, Authors and Settings always do. Paper tables sets the visible columns, their widths and where the DOI is shown.

items.title: Library
items.text:
• Home feed: the feeds on the home page and how long entries are kept. See Home feed.
  • Feed filters: DENY and ALLOW rules for feed entries.
  • Search: whether search terms are saved for autocomplete, and how many.
  • Metadata lookup: which sources are on and the default one.
  • Contacts & API keys: contact addresses sent to arXiv, Crossref and OpenAlex, and the NCBI key for PubMed. Values set as environment variables take precedence.
  • Full-text index: the background worker that fetches and indexes TeX source for saved arXiv papers.
  • PDF full text: indexes PDF text for papers without TeX source.
  • arXiv version monitoring: checks saved arXiv papers for newer versions.
  • PDF folders: arranges the PDF folder by year, journal, or both, with a preview before any file moves.

items.title: Server & data
items.text: Storage sets a cap on total PDF size; downloads and imports stop once saved PDFs reach it. Login changes your password and can log out every other session. Backup downloads, imports or restores the database of the library you are looking at, and exports or imports its settings as a JSON file. Logs shows the server log, and Activity lists every change made through the API, with the account that made it in multi-user mode.

items.title: AI
items.text:
Switch AI features on, choose a provider, model and key, and test the connection. Author ORCIDs fills in missing ORCIDs. See AI features.

API keys are write-only. After saving, the page shows only their last 4 characters.

items.title: Integrations
items.text: The MCP server for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode: switch it on, choose the tool profile and create the access token. See MCP server.

items.title: Browser add-on
items.text: The Browser add-on card creates the access token for the linXiv Firefox add-on. Each account has its own token, shown once. Papers it saves go to your library and onto the reading list Imported - to check. See Browser add-on.

items.title: Server Admin
items.text:
Admins only. Multi-user mode turns named accounts and the shared library on or off, and Users adds, edits and deletes accounts. Maintenance operations finds duplicate papers, completes metadata of new papers, checks PDF files, backs up the databases, removes authors and tags without papers and empties old trash, on demand or nightly. See Server Admin and Maintenance operations.

In multi-user mode, accounts that are not admins see fewer settings: no MCP card, Server Admin group, Logs card or Activity card, and About shows the version only. Their AI keys, contacts, feeds and lookup choices belong to their own library.

items.title: About
items.text: Version, update check against the published image (by hand or daily, weekly or monthly), health warnings about the configuration, disk space used by the data, PDF and log folders, and a diagnostics report for bug reports.

items.title: Trash
items.text:
Deleting a paper or project moves it to the Trash. Deleted papers stay there until you restore them or delete them forever, and a restored paper comes back with its PDF and project links. Deleted projects are listed below the papers and can be restored the same way.

Delete forever asks you to confirm and cannot be undone.

items.title: Backups
items.text:
Settings → Server & data → Backup has these actions:

  • Download a backup: a snapshot of the database (papers, metadata, tags, projects, notes and authors). Saved PDF files are not included.
  • Import: merges another linXiv database into this library.
  • Restore: replaces the library with the backup. It is refused while a background job runs.
  • Download settings / Import settings: every setting a Save can change, as a JSON file. API keys and tokens are left out of the file and stay as they are when you import one.

Admins can also keep backups on the server, made nightly or on demand: see Database backups on the server. The Empty trash maintenance operation deletes papers that have been in the trash longer than a set number of days (1 to 120).

Back up the PDF folder separately. Self-hosting shows which folders to copy.

items.title: HTTP API
items.text:
The web UI uses this API, and scripts can call it too. Every route except /api/health, /api/login, /api/me, /mcp and the add-on routes /api/clip/ping, /api/clip/pdf and /api/clip/bibtex needs a session when a password is set. Write requests also need the X-CSRF-Token header, which echoes the lxw_csrf cookie.

Most routes map to one linxiv CLI command. The right column names the command or describes what the server does.

In multi-user mode (see Server Admin) each request works on the caller's own library, or on the shared library when it sends the header X-Linxiv-Library: shared (plain links such as a PDF or a download use ?library=shared instead). Writes to the shared library by accounts that are not admins get 403, except POST /api/shared/copy and POST /api/export/bibtex. Logs, activity, update check, system status and diagnostics, and /api/mcp are admin only. Add-on routes with the bearer token always work on the token owner's own library and ignore this header. They accept requests with no Origin or a moz-extension:// one, and answer 403 to any other Origin. GET /api/jobs lists only the caller's own jobs for accounts that are not admins.

Route linxiv command / behaviour POST /api/login {username?, password, remember?} Start a session. username is required in multi-user mode and ignored otherwise; failed attempts are limited per client address and username GET /api/me Login state: auth_enabled, setup_required, authenticated, password_source, multi_user, username, role (admin or user), owner POST /api/password {current, new, remember?} Change the caller's own password; logs out the caller's other sessions. For the owner this is the stored server password (409 when it comes from LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD(_HASH)). In multi-user mode the new password must differ from every other account's GET /api/admin/multi-user, POST /api/admin/multi-user {enabled, username?} Admin only. Multi-user status and owner username; turn it on (username names the owner the first time) or off (owner only; logs out every other account) GET /api/users, POST /api/users {username, password, role} Admin only. List accounts (never their password hashes); create one with its own library (409 for a taken username, 400 for a password another account uses) PUT /api/users/{id} {username?, password?, role?}, DELETE /api/users/{id} Admin only. Rename, set a password, change the role (each ends that account's sessions); delete (the library stays on disk, its path is returned). The owner stays admin and can't be deleted; the last admin can't be demoted or deleted; nobody deletes their own account POST /api/shared/copy {source_ids} Copy papers with their PDFs from the shared library into the caller's own: a temporary project is exported with project export --pdfs and imported with project import --on-conflict=merge, then both temporary projects are deleted. Returns copied, failed, skipped_pdfs POST /api/sessions/revoke-others Log out every session except the caller's; returns {revoked} GET /api/activity?limit, GET /api/activity/export Activity log, newest first / as CSV: every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE under /api/ with time, client address, route, path parameters, status (Settings saves: key names only). Kept in <data dir>/logs/activity.jsonl, 5 MiB + one rotated file DELETE /api/activity {confirm: "delete activity log"} Clear the activity log (the clear is recorded) GET /api/system/diagnostics Markdown report for bug reports: versions, configuration, library counts, disk, health, running jobs, DNS + TCP 443 reachability of outside services. Secrets and addresses that could locate the server only as set / not set GET /api/search?q&source=arxiv\|openalex\|crossref&max search POST /api/papers/{id}/fetch?source= fetch, then paper get GET /api/papers?q&tag&pdf=has\|none&fulltext&limit&offset&category&sort&dir list filtered server-side; a q of 3+ characters also runs paper search (TeX full text and notes), hits flagged deep_match; fulltext=true returns only the paper search hits. Each paper also gets pdf_file (its PDF's path inside the PDF folder) and title_suspect (the title looks like junk read from the PDF, or unlike the file name) GET /api/papers/{id}, GET /api/papers/{id}/versions paper get (plus pdf_file, title_suspect, bib (stored BibTeX fields, {} when none) and metadata_source ({source, ref} or null)), paper versions DELETE /api/papers/{id} paper delete (soft delete, goes to trash) GET /api/papers/{id}/pdf pdf path, then serves the file (only from inside the data or PDF dir) POST /api/papers/{id}/pdf {url?, version?} pdf download (for arXiv papers the URL is derived) DELETE /api/papers/{id}/pdf pdf delete PUT /api/papers/{id}/metadata {title, authors[], published, summary, category?, doi?, url?, tags?, bib?, metadata_source?} paper get, then paper repair with the full record and the paper's current tags (repair clears any field it isn't given). bib sets BibTeX fields linXiv has no column for (entry_type, booktitle, editor, edition, series, volume, number, chapter, pages, month, publisher, address, school, institution, organization, howpublished, note, issn, isbn, eprint, archive_prefix, primary_class; null clears one) in the web server's per-library linxiv-web-bib.db. metadata_source {source, ref} records where the values came from (crossref, pubmed, biorxiv, arxiv, openalex, bibtex, filename, ai); a Crossref or OpenAlex source without bib has its fields read from that API GET /api/papers/{id}/lookup?source=crossref\|arxiv\|openalex\|pubmed\|biorxiv&by=auto\|filename Candidate metadata: doi resolve (by DOI), search (by arXiv id or title), NCBI E-utilities for PubMed (by DOI, then title), api.biorxiv.org (by DOI). by=filename searches by the title in the PDF's file name, ignoring the stored DOI, and adds a last candidate built from the file name and its year folder. Each candidate carries bib, its BibTeX fields or null; for a Crossref DOI match they are read from api.crossref.org /works/{doi} GET/POST/DELETE /api/papers/{id}/tags tag list / tag add / tag remove GET /api/pdfs, GET /api/pdfs/storage pdf list, pdf storage (recounted including subfolders) POST /api/pdfs/import (multipart file) pdf import GET /api/pdfs/layout/preview?layout=, POST /api/jobs/pdf-layout PDF folder layout (none, year, journal, year/journal, journal/year): preview, then a job that moves files and updates their stored path POST /api/import/bibtex, POST /api/import/zotero (multipart file) bibtex import, zotero import (upsert: existing entries are updated) POST /api/add {input} arXiv id/link: fetch; DOI or doi.org link: doi save; other http(s) link: server downloads the PDF (public hosts only, size-capped), then pdf import GET /api/stats, /api/categories, /api/tags stats, categories, tag list-all GET /api/authors?hide_single, GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/authors/{id} author list, author get, author update, author delete (409 while linked to papers) GET /api/authors/{id}/merge-candidates, POST /api/authors/{id}/merge author merge-candidates (plus same-name hints), author merge POST /api/orcid/backfill {limit?} orcid backfill (1 to 100; 409 while one runs) GET /api/projects?status=active\|archived, POST /api/projects, PATCH /api/projects/{id} project list, project create, project update GET /api/projects/{id}, GET /api/projects/{id}/papers project get; papers = project get + list, filtered to members in project order POST /api/projects/{id}/papers ({"source_ids": [...]}), DELETE /api/projects/{id}/papers/{source_id} project add-papers (200 with added/failed), project remove-paper GET /api/projects/{id}/export?format=lxproj\|bibtex\|obsidian\|zotero&pdfs project export [--pdfs], export-bibtex, export-obsidian, export-zotero; written to a temp dir, sent as a download, then deleted POST /api/projects/import/preview, POST /api/projects/import (multipart file, on_conflict=merge\|overwrite) project import --preview, project import (.lxproj, zip checked before the CLI sees it) POST /api/projects/{id}/archive, POST /api/projects/{id}/restore, DELETE /api/projects/{id} project archive, project restore, project delete (soft delete, goes to trash) GET /api/notes?paper=&project=, POST /api/notes, PATCH /api/notes/{id}, DELETE /api/notes/{id} note list, note create [--project-id], note update, note delete (permanent); title/content capped at 100 kB GET /api/annotations?paper=&project=, POST /api/annotations, PATCH /api/annotations/{id}, DELETE /api/annotations/{id} annotation list/create/update/delete (PDF highlights; anchors validated server-side) GET /api/graph Knowledge graph of papers, authors and tags, built from list and author list GET /api/graph/export The same graph as a file: format=graphml (default) or format=csv (zip of nodes.csv and edges.csv); exclude_single_authors=true drops single-paper authors GET /api/feed, POST /api/feed/dismiss feed get for the stored home feed URL (cached 5 minutes), feed dismiss GET /api/feed/rules, POST /api/feed/rules, DELETE /api/feed/rules/{id} feed rules list/add/delete GET /api/versions/new, POST /api/versions/check {limit?}, POST /api/versions/{id}/ack versions new, versions check --limit (1 to 100, default 20; stores new versions it finds), versions ack (a second ack still returns ok) POST /api/papers/{id}/source {force?} paper fetch-source [--force]: downloads the paper's arXiv LaTeX source and indexes its text for full-text search (400 for non-arXiv papers) GET /api/sources/pending, GET /api/sources/worker Saved arXiv papers whose source isn't indexed; status of the background full-text indexer POST /api/jobs/index-sources {limit?}, GET /api/jobs?kind=, GET /api/jobs/{id}, POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel Background job: one paper fetch-source per pending paper, 7 s apart (409 if one is already running) GET /api/trash trash list POST /api/trash/papers/{id}/restore, DELETE /api/trash/papers/{id} trash restore, trash hard-delete (paper must be in the trash) POST /api/trash/projects/{id}/restore, DELETE /api/trash/projects/{id} trash restore-project, trash hard-delete-project GET /api/backup, POST /api/backup/import, POST /api/backup/restore (multipart file) backup (database snapshot download), import (merge another database), restore (replace the library; refused while a job runs) GET /api/settings/export, POST /api/settings/import (the exported JSON) Settings that PATCH /api/settings accepts, as a download without API keys or tokens (admins also get the server-wide keys); import applies a file's settings through the same checks, refusing API keys and unknown keys GET /api/maintenance, PUT /api/maintenance/schedule {hour, nightly[], monthly[]?, keep_backups?, trash_days? (0-120)}, POST /api/maintenance/{op}/run Admin only. Maintenance operations (duplicates, complete-metadata, metadata-refresh, pdf-check, backup, clean-authors, clean-tags, empty-trash) with their last result and running job; the nightly hour (server local time) and the operations ticked nightly or monthly (monthly: at that hour once 30 days have passed since the last run); start one as job maint-<op> over every library (409 while it runs) GET /api/maintenance/backups, GET/DELETE /api/maintenance/backups/{library}/{name} Admin only. Database backups the backup operation keeps in each library's maintenance/backups/: list, download, delete GET/PUT /api/maintenance/complete-metadata/options {gaps[], sources[]} Admin only. Which gaps (title, authors, date, abstract, journal, doi) make a new paper incomplete, and which sources (arxiv, biorxiv, crossref, pubmed) are asked, in order; at least one of each GET/PUT /api/maintenance/metadata-refresh/options {scope} Admin only. Which papers metadata-refresh asks again: recent_or_preprint (published within a year, or arXiv / bioRxiv / medRxiv; default) or all GET /api/maintenance/pdf-check Admin only. Last pdf-check report per library: missing PDF files and files no paper points at (lists capped at 500, counts complete), plus disk (files of any type, PDFs, skipped, per top-level folder) and paper counts (papers, papers_with_pdf, extra_versions, trashed_pdfs) GET/PUT /api/maintenance/pdf-check/options {skip: [folder]} Admin only. Top-level folders of the PDF folder the check counts but never lists as unlinked (max 20; orphans always skipped) GET /api/maintenance/pdf-check/{library}/unlinked.tsv, /missing.tsv Admin only. Every unlinked file (file, size, modified) or every paper with a missing PDF (source_id, version, title) of the last check, tab separated POST /api/maintenance/pdf-check/{library}/move-orphans Admin only. Job pdf-orphans: checks again, moves unlinked PDFs older than one hour to orphans/<same path> ((n) suffix on clash), nothing deleted; 409 while another job runs GET /api/duplicates, POST /api/duplicates/merge {winner, loser}, POST /api/duplicates/dismiss {source_ids}, GET /api/duplicates/export.tsv Groups of papers with identical PDF files from the last duplicates run in this library; paper merge keeps the winner; dismissed groups stay hidden on later runs; the TSV has one row per paper (group, sha256, source_id, version, title, file, size) GET /api/metadata-review, POST /api/metadata-review/remove {source_ids} Papers complete-metadata could not complete in this library (fixed or deleted ones drop out); take papers off the list GET /api/settings, PATCH /api/settings settings get, settings update, limited to an allowlist (storage cap, TeX rendering, contact addresses, home feed, search history, full-text worker, AI and MCP settings); API keys are write-only GET /api/ai/models, POST /api/ai/test, GET /api/ai/schemas Provider model list, connection test, the JSON Schema and example each AI action uses (409 while AI is off) POST /api/ai/tags/{id}, POST /api/ai/summary/{id}?pdf=, POST /api/ai/cleanup/{id} AI tag suggestions, summary, metadata cleanup; previews only, nothing is written GET /api/mcp, POST /api/mcp/token, DELETE /api/mcp/token MCP status, create (shown once) or revoke the access token POST/GET/DELETE /mcp MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint (bearer token; see MCP server) GET /api/clip/token, POST /api/clip/token, DELETE /api/clip/token Browser add-on token of the caller's library: status, create (shown once; replaces any previous one) or revoke. Every account has its own GET /api/clip/list {project_id} of the add-on's reading list in this library, null before the first clip GET /api/clip/ping Add-on token. {ok, version, username} POST /api/clip/pdf (multipart file) Add-on token. Trial pdf import in a throwaway library to learn the id. New paper or no PDF yet: pdf import (metadata of an existing paper put back with paper repair). Has a PDF: no import. Then project add-papers to the list. Answers {source_ids, new, existing, attached, project_id, failed}, plus title when known and metadata_kept when a PDF was attached to an existing paper POST /api/clip/bibtex (multipart file) Add-on token. bibtex import of the entries not in the library, matched by DOI, arXiv id, else exact title, then project add-papers for all of them. Answers {source_ids, new, existing, project_id, failed}

Paper ids are linXiv source ids such as arxiv:1706.03762. Old-style arXiv ids keep their slash: /api/papers/arxiv:hep-th/9901001.

items.title: linXiv versions
items.text:
linXiv-web linXiv CLI / MCP 0.1.x v0.7.1

The image builds linxiv and linxiv-mcp from upstream source at the LINXIV_REF build arg (default v0.7.1).

items.title: Resource usage
items.text:
Measured on a home server (Intel i7-7560U, 4 threads, 16 GB RAM) with a library of about 6,000 papers, 6,000 PDFs and 2,000 tags:

Image size 357 MB on disk (91 MB compressed) Memory, idle 155–185 MiB Memory, peak 302 MiB CPU, idle under 1% Data dir (papers.db, logs, state) 16 MB PDFs 12 GB (on a separate USB disk)

No CPU or memory limits were set.

items.title: Bare metal requirements
items.text:
Not supported, but feasible without code changes. Docker is the tested path. Running directly on a host needs:

  • linxiv and linxiv-mcp built from the linXiv repo at v0.7.1 (Rust toolchain, cargo build --release -p linxiv-cli -p linxiv-mcp), on PATH or set with LINXIV_BIN / LINXIV_MCP_BIN
  • PDFium library from linXiv's scripts/fetch_pdfium.sh, with LINXIV_PDFIUM_LIB set to its path
  • Python 3.11+ and uv for the server (cd server && uv sync --frozen --no-dev)
  • Node.js and npm to build the web UI once (cd web && npm ci && npm run build), with LINXIV_WEB_STATIC_DIR set to web/dist
  • Data and PDF directories, with LINXIV_DATA_DIR and LINXIV_WEB_DATA_DIR set to the same path, plus LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR
  • <data dir>/pdfs linked to the PDF directory, as entrypoint.sh does in the container
  • LINXIV_WEB_HOST set for network access (the default is 127.0.0.1)
  • A service manager (systemd, launchd) to run python -m app as a non-root user and restart it

items.title: PDF folder on an SMB share
items.text:
Not tested on SMB, but the design allows it. Only the data dir must stay on a local disk.

Key points:

  • Ownership: the container runs as uid 1000 and CIFS ignores chown. Mount with uid=1000,gid=1000,file_mode=0644,dir_mode=0755.
  • Mount the share on the host (/etc/fstab or systemd, with _netdev,nofail) and bind-mount it as /pdfs, rather than using Docker's CIFS volume driver.
  • Start order: the server refuses to start when the PDF folder is missing, which stops writes into an empty mount point. Start the container after the mount, for example with x-systemd.automount.
  • Share offline: if the NAS sleeps or the network drops, PDF reads, imports and downloads fail, and on a hard mount they can hang until LINXIV_WEB_TIMEOUT_LONG (120 s). Library data is not affected.
  • Speed: opening PDFs, the full-text indexer and layout moves run at network speed. The rest of the app does not touch the PDF folder.
  • File names: with the "by journal" layout, SMB may reject or change characters in journal names that a Linux filesystem accepts.

items.title: Admin Server Configuration
items.text:
linXiv-web reads these environment variables, usually from the .env file next to docker-compose.yml.

Variable Default Purpose LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH none argon2 hash of the login password (python -m app hash-password). Without it (or LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD), first-run setup in the browser creates the password, stored in <data dir>/linxiv-web-auth.json LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD none Plain password, hashed in memory at startup (dev only) LINXIV_WEB_SECRET_KEY generated, kept in <data dir>/linxiv-web-state.db Session signing key. Changing it logs everyone out LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE false Set to true behind HTTPS LINXIV_WEB_HSTS false Send Strict-Transport-Security (1 year). Only behind HTTPS: browsers then refuse plain HTTP to this host LINXIV_WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS 90 Login lifetime when "Remember me" is ticked (otherwise the login lasts until the browser closes, at most 14 days) LINXIV_WEB_DATA_DIR /data linXiv data dir (papers.db). Passed to the CLI and MCP server as LINXIV_DATA_DIR LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR /pdfs PDF directory, symlinked from <data dir>/pdfs LINXIV_WEB_LIBRARIES_PDF_DIR none Multi-user mode: where the shared and per-account libraries keep their PDFs (<dir>/<library>). Unset: inside each library's folder under <data dir>/libraries/. Must be writable and not inside LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR. See Server Admin LINXIV_WEB_HOST / LINXIV_WEB_PORT 0.0.0.0 / 8000 in the image Listen address LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL false Serve clients with public IP addresses. Off: only loopback, private LAN and link-local clients get through (others get 403) LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES none Comma-separated IPs/CIDRs of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is believed (read right to left). Unlisted proxies count as the client LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB 200 Upload size cap LINXIV_WEB_LOG_LEVEL info App log level at startup: debug, info, warning or error. A level saved in Settings → Logs overrides it TZ UTC Time zone for the nightly maintenance hour and the times shown for maintenance runs and server backups, e.g. Europe/London. See Maintenance operations LINXIV_WEB_TIMEOUT_LONG / _SHORT 120 / 30 CLI timeout in seconds (search, fetch, download and import use the long one) LINXIV_BIN / LINXIV_MCP_BIN linxiv / linxiv-mcp CLI and MCP server binaries ARXIV_MAILTO, CROSSREF_MAILTO, OPENALEX_MAILTO none Contact addresses sent to those services; override the values set in Settings NCBI_API_KEY none PubMed key; overrides the one set in Settings GHCR_TOKEN none GitHub token with read:packages for the update check, needed only if the image on ghcr.io is private; overrides the one set in Settings GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GENAI_API_KEY_TAG_GEN none AI provider keys (the last one is for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint); override the ones set in Settings LINXIV_WEB_AI_ALLOWED_HOSTS none Comma-separated host names the OpenAI-compatible base URL may use. Unset: any host except cloud metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fd00:ec2::254, 100.100.100.200), which are always refused

Keys entered in Settings are stored in the linXiv settings store. The server never sends them back to the browser, only their last 4 characters.

The Compose file also reads LINXIV_WEB_BIND, LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT, LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST and LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST to decide where the port is published and which host folders are mounted. Self-hosting explains them.
